rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for chewing food.

example.english: You have to chew this meat slowly before you can swallow it.
example.traditional: 呢啲肉要慢慢咬，先至吞得落。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 juk6 jiu3 maan6 maan6 ngaau5 sin1 zi3 tan1 dak1 lok6

rows.note: Use this for thinking something over rather than physically chewing it.

example.english: I’ll chew this matter over again when I get home.
example.traditional: 呢件事我返屋企再諗下先。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 ngo5 faan1 uk1 kei2 zoi3 nam2 haa5 sin1

rows.note: Use this when teeth have chewed something up or damaged it.

example.english: I saw the dog chew up my sneakers.
example.jyutping: zek3 gau2 ngaau5 laan6 zo2 ngo5 deoi3 bo1 haai4

rows.note: Use this formal phrase specifically for the practice of chewing tobacco.

example.english: Some workers used to chew tobacco to stay alert.
example.traditional: 以前有啲工人會咀嚼煙草嚟提神。
example.jyutping: ji5 cin4 jau5 di1 gung1 jan4 wui5 zeoi2 zoek3 jin1 cou2 lei4 tai4 san4
